items.title: Morning Briefing: Nov. 10
items.excerpt: Iclal Turan 10 November 2026• Update: 10 November 2026 WASHINGTON Here’s a rundown of all the news you need to start your Tuesday, including US President Donald Trump saying further military action against Iran “doesn’t seem to be a very necessary thing,” COP31 entering 2nd day with focus on energy, transport, and a new round of US-brokered Russia-Ukraine trilateral peace beginning Tuesday. US President Donald Trump said further military action against Iran did not appear necessary at this stage, while warning that Washington remained prepared to act if the situation changed. "At this point, taking the military action doesn't seem to be a very necessary thing — but we're locked and loaded, ready to go for any reason," he told reporters at the White House. Trump added that Israel and the wider Middle East were protected from the Iranian "danger and threat." "We're seeing momentum toward the end of this conflict. I think it's going to be ending fairly soon," he said. - COP31 enters 2nd day with focus on energy, transport The UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) entered its second day in Türkiye on Tuesday, with discussions focusing on energy security, electrification, grid infrastructure and sustainable transport. According to the conference program, around 370 sessions are scheduled throughout the day, including 140 under the energy and transport theme. In the Blue Zone, which hosts official negotiations and high-level meetings, key events include a ministerial meeting on the Azerbaijan–Kazakhstan–Uzbekistan green energy partnership, as well as panel discussion on green energy security and Ukraine's energy transition. Other Blue Zone sessions will address energy security amid geopolitical risks, financing the energy transition and expanding renewable energy infrastructure. Meanwhile, the Green Zone, which opened to visitors Monday, will host discussions on sustainable mobility, clean energy investment and industrial decarbonization. - New round of US-brokered Russia-Ukraine trilateral peace to begin today A new round of US-brokered Russia-Ukraine trilateral peace talks in Abu Dhabi to begin Tuesday. Russia and Ukraine last held US-mediated peace talks earlier this year, with three rounds taking place on Jan. 23-24, Feb. 4-5 and Feb. 17-18. The first two were held in Abu Dhabi, while the third took place in Geneva. A Russian delegation arrived in the Emirati capital Abu Dhabi on Monday to participate in trilateral talks involving Russia, Ukraine and the United States, the state-run Tass news agency reported. The delegation is led by presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky, while Ukraine's delegation will be led by Rustem Umerov, the head of the country's Foreign Intelligence Service. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said the talks would focus on security guarantees, adding that European representatives would not participate because the negotiations were initially agreed upon as a trilateral format. ... - Shares of US chipmaker Nvidia plunged 6.4% to $174.7 after its board launched an independent investigation into reports that CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. - US President Donald Trump said he spoke with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who told him he had no idea that a businesswoman he was reportedly close to was a spy. - China dismissed allegations of a Chinese spy plot targeting Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as “unsubstantiated” and “nothing but smears” against the country.

items.title: The Christian Science Monitor Daily for November 10, 2026
items.excerpt: Rep. Thomas Massie of Kentucky launched a bid to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. He filed a resolution in the House of Representatives. It included eight articles of impeachment. The action sets the stage for a vote on whether to remove one of the Trump administration’s most prominent figures following sweeping midterm election losses. The resolution largely focuses on the war in Iran, but also includes references to Mr. Hegseth’s role in carrying out military actions in Yemen and Venezuela. A vote in the House could come by mid-week. – The Associated Press US-mediated talks on ending Russia-Ukraine war began. Russia, Ukraine, and the United States have started three-way talks in the United Arab Emirates. The discussions Tuesday mark the first meeting since February. The U.S. is pushing for a resolution to the war which began with Russia’s invasion in February 2022. Russian President Vladimir Putin demands Ukraine pull back troops and abandon its NATO bid. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy rejects these terms. Both sides remain far apart on key issues. Russia and Ukraine have intensified aerial attacks, including long-range strikes with drones and missiles. – AP Our coverage: Ukraine peace momentum builds, but Russia sticks to its guns 1,156 U.S. schools shut down during the 2025-26 academic year. Experts say the rise in closures – the highest number since the pandemic – reflects declining birth rates, shrinking public school enrollment, and growing financial pressures on school districts. A shift by a growing number of families to private or charter schools or to homeschooling has added to the enrollment decline, according to an investigation published on Monday by The Associated Press, The Hechinger Report, and Stanford University’s Big Local News. Researchers warn that further closures are likely as districts struggle to adjust. The Supreme Court cleared the way for border wall construction in Texas’s Big Bend to resume. The wall is a key project for President Donald Trump, who promised to build it from the Pacific Ocean to the Gulf of Mexico. Republicans in Congress funded the project with $46 billion last summer. Customs and Border Protection have been building 12 miles of border barriers a week. In the Big Bend region, bipartisan opposition argues the project wastes money in an area with historically low illegal immigration and suggests using surveillance technology instead. – AP New Zealanders will have to wait for weeks to discover who will lead the country after Saturday’s election. The right-leaning National Party coalition was hoping to cling on to power but, in the tightest result in years, neither of the main parties won enough seats for victory. Opportunity, a centrist party led by political newcomer Qiulae Wong, won seven seats. Ms. Wong has said she could work with either the National Party or the left-leaning Labour Party to form a government. A decision’s not expected until Nov. 27.

items.title: Speech by Governor Waller on the economic outlook - Federal Reserve Board
items.excerpt: November 10, 2026 ### The Economic Outlook and Some Thoughts on Labor Market Dynamism Governor Christopher J. Waller At the Bank of England Watchers Conference King’s Business School and Money, Macro and Finance Society, London, United Kingdom ... My subject today is the outlook for the U.S. economy and the implications for monetary policy. I think there is little disagreement about the basics of that outlook. The U.S. economy is growing strongly, with a labor market that has brought employment close to its long-term rate. But inflation remains too high, so I will explain why I believe further tightening of monetary policy will be needed, sooner rather than later, to return inflation to a path that will reach 2 percent in the medium term. ... Let me turn to the economy. Economic output continues to grow at a healthy pace. The initial estimate was that real gross domestic product (GDP) rose 3.4 percent in the third quarter, supported by strong consumer spending and robust investment. Consumption growth was helped by a booming stock market, and investment by businesses continued to surge, especially in high-tech equipment associated with the artificial intelligence (AI) buildout. I expect GDP growth is backing off a bit in the current quarter, as consumer spending slows to levels that I think are more consistent with household income and wealth, but output will continue to grow at a solid pace. The labor market has also been solid. The unemployment rate ticked down to 4.1 percent in October, the same rate it was over the summer. Job creation, which has been fluctuating widely month to month for some time, saw October gains of 165,000 jobs and 85,000 jobs added to estimates of the previous two months. To look through the volatility, the 6-month and 12-month average payroll gains have been closer to 80,000 jobs a month. This level is a bit above most estimates of the breakeven level needed to keep the unemployment rate steady but entirely consistent with my view that the supply and demand for labor are in rough balance. ... By contrast, inflation is well above 2 percent and the focus of my attention. For reasons I explained at the start of this speech, I was willing to wait to tighten monetary policy at the FOMC's October meeting. Inconveniently for today's event, we will get consumer price index (CPI) inflation for October in a few hours. While I am hoping for an improvement over September, even if this occurs, I would still support a 25 basis point increase in the FOMC's policy rate at our December meeting. However, if inflation comes in substantially higher than I expect, more robust action by the FOMC may be called for. Let's just say it. September's inflation data were bad. There was no silver lining. Inflation based on personal consumption expenditures (PCE), the measure targeted by the FOMC, rose at a monthly rate of 0.5 percent in September and 3.7 percent over the previous 12 months. Core PCE inflation, excluding food and energy prices, rose 0.3 percent in September and 3.1 percent from that time last year. Both these measures are too high, and I am particularly concerned about the breadth of price increases. Earlier this year, excessive inflation was driven by nonmarket prices that are estimated rather than observed by the government, and ones that I tend to discount as hard to measure and as an unreliable guide to the overall trend for core inflation. But now, two components with greater relevance to future inflation are elevated—core goods prices and those for core market-based services excluding housing. More than 70 percent of the components of core PCE service prices saw 12-month increases above 3 percent in September. Later today, I will be looking to see whether this breadth of elevated inflation continues, including whether high-tech goods prices related to the AI buildout continue to rise at the very high rate of recent months. I also want to know if the run-up in energy prices of the past several months is being passed through to goods and services directly or indirectly, because of higher input costs. While I am pleased to see energy prices down from their high rates over the past week or so, they are still quite elevated relative to the start of the year, and the ultimate effect on inflation will depend on what levels are sustained. Federal Reserve staff have been thinking hard about the effects on inflation of the AI buildout and elevated energy prices, and their findings do not encourage me to think that these factors will be fading anytime soon. ... Some other Fed research indicates to me that energy price pressures may pass through to goods and services in a more sustained way than in the past. 7 The researchers find a potential shift in the inflation process after the pandemic that suggests core inflation may be more responsive to energy shocks. Central bankers have tended to look through energy price shocks and expect that their effects on inflation will soon fade, but this new work cautions against taking too much comfort in this view. Their analysis suggests that, especially if oil prices were to remain elevated, these pressures could be larger than previously though and persist well into 2027. ... To recap my economic outlook, economic activity is strong, the labor market is stable, but inflation is too high, well above the FOMC's 2 percent goal. This means that even if, as I expect, the monthly rate of inflation improves in October, I am leaning toward supporting an increase in our policy rate of 25 basis points at the FOMC's December meeting. That's my plan if things proceed as I expect. But if the October CPI inflation data out later today are similar to the past two monthly readings—with core CPI inflation around 0.3 percent or even higher—then a stronger policy move may be needed. In that case, I believe a 50 basis point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting. Hiking only 25 basis points would put our credibility at risk, a risk I am not eager to take.

items.title: US consumer prices expected to have risen at slower pace in October By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 10 (Reuters) - US consumer prices likely increased at a moderate pace in October, but inflation probably remained stubbornly high, leaving the Federal Reserve on course to raise interest rates next month. The anticipated slowdown in the Consumer Price Index would largely reflect a retreat in gasoline prices. The Labor Department’s Bureau of Labor Statistics will not publish year-over-year inflation readings when it releases the report on Tuesday because last year’s federal government shutdown prevented the collection of consumer price data in October 2025, leaving no comparison base. Annual consumer inflation jumped 3.7% in September, and economists said they had no reason to expect it to have cooled in October even if the pace of increase slowed over the month. Inflation is running well above the US central bank’s 2% target. The US-Israeli war with Iran has boosted oil prices, combining with the import tariffs implemented by the Trump administration last year to lift the cost of living. High inflation contributed to the heavy losses suffered by President Donald Trump’s Republican Party in the midterm elections last week. "What you will see in the data is further evidence of stubborn and sticky inflation, especially in the service sector," said Joseph Brusuelas, chief economist at RSM. "That will result in a December rate hike, and I do not expect the October CPI data to dislodge the Fed from that monetary path." The CPI likely increased 0.3% last month after accelerating by 0.6% in September, a Reuters survey of economists predicted. Though oil prices rose over the month, retail gasoline prices fell 0.9% from September, before adjustment for seasonal fluctuations, data from the US Energy Information Administration showed. Economists anticipated a small increase in gasoline prices in the CPI report after the seasonal adjustment. That move would follow a 9.1% surge in September. Food prices are also expected to have risen after being unchanged in September. TAME CORE CPI ANTICIPATED Excluding the volatile food and energy components, the CPI is forecast to have increased 0.2% after gaining 0.3% in September. The so-called core CPI was likely restrained last month by a deceleration or even decline in the cost of airfares. But prices for hotel and motel rooms probably remained high, as did owners’ equivalent rent, a measure of the amount homeowners would pay to rent or would earn from renting their property. The BLS will update the data used to calculate the health insurance components, which some economists expected would result in subdued readings. An artificial intelligence investment boom is expected to keep prices for information technology goods higher. In the absence of last year’s inflation data, some economists used the average index for September and November 2025 to estimate the year-over-year rate of change for the October CPI. Others used interpolated levels from independent sources. Their estimates for the October CPI converged at a 3.9% year-over-year increase. Core CPI inflation was projected to have increased 2.7% in the 12 months through October after advancing 2.6% in September. The missing data from last year have no impact on the calculation of the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index readings that are tracked by the Fed to gauge progress toward its inflation target. Both measures are running above 3%. Late on Monday, financial markets were pricing in a roughly 85% chance of a rate hike next month. The Fed left its benchmark overnight interest rate in the 3.75%-4.00% range last month. "The main risk for Fed officials not following through on a December rate hike would be a further substantial correction in equity markets or widening credit spreads," said Veronica Clark, an economist at Citigroup.

items.title: Up First briefing: Pete Hegseth; Trump on Iran; Nvidia; Texas border : NPR
items.excerpt: November 10, 2026 7:01 AM ET ... The House may vote this week on a resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Rep. Thomas Massie, R-KY, reintroduced articles of impeachment accusing Hegseth of high crimes and misdemeanors. The eight specific charges include three charges for illegally waging war against Iran, one for ignoring laws to minimize civilian casualties, one for overseeing extrajudicial killings of alleged drug boats in the Caribbean and Eastern Pacific, and one for capturing Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro without congressional authorization. Hegseth has called the articles a sham. ... - 🎧 Only a few Republicans need to support impeachment in the House for it to be possible, NPR's Sam Gringlas tells Up First. This would lead to a Senate trial. Removing Hegseth from the Pentagon requires 67 senators, which will be challenging even once Democrats take control. But Massie told reporters he believes it will be possible, and opposition to the war in his fellow Republicans' home states could convince them to get on board. Massie says some members of Congress have come around to the idea that the administration must be held accountable for violating congressional war powers - ➡️ Also on House Republicans' agenda: a closed-door meeting today to pick a minority leader for the next Congress. The decision is down to current House Majority Leader Steve Scalise, R-La., and Ohio's Jim Jordan, a co-founder of the far-right House Freedom Caucus. President Trump has acknowledged that the war he initiated with Iran harmed his party in the midterms. Weeks before the election, the president said he was going to hold off on any strikes in Iran. While campaigning, he hinted at potential actions to proceed with the war and teased a significant move to end it. Now, Trump says there's no need for further strikes if talks are ongoing. - 🎧 NPR's Deepa Shivaram says it's possible that Trump might resume military action if he doesn't get the deal he wants, because he has shown a pattern of shifting on his rhetoric since the war began. The president has also insisted that the war was necessary and he would do it again. Shivaram says Trump is starting to shift focus to shape his legacy in these last two years of his presidency. He is trying to frame the unpopular war as a success by saying Iran's nuclear stock is eliminated and that was his goal. In the remainder of his time in office, he wants to establish himself as a dealmaker and peacemaker. ... The U.S. Supreme Court yesterday gave the Trump administration the green light to proceed with plans to build hundreds of miles of border barriers and security infrastructure in west Texas. The decision was made despite ongoing court hearings. This plan has faced bipartisan backlash for its involvement of Big Bend National Park, a cherished area known for its stunning canyons and pristine desert landscape. In a five-page decision, the Court asserted that the federal judge who issued an injunction against the construction lacked the authority to intervene.

items.title: Trump backs Nvidia’s Jensen Huang and Republicans select new congressional leaders: Morning Rundown
items.excerpt: ## Trump defends Jensen Huang as investigates Nvidia Less than a day after tech company Nvidia said it launched an investigation into Jensen Huang’s extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump expressed his support for the embattled CEO as details emerged about a Commerce Department investigation that was abruptly paused. Trump said at an impromptu news conference yesterday that the FBI is now investigating Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, the managing director of Singaporean tech company Megaspeed. The pair are not related. U.S. intelligence agencies now believe she is a Chinese spy. Trump said he called Huang “to see if he’s feeling all right,” and Huang told him “he had absolutely no idea that person was a spy.” Trump added, “I really believe him.” Meanwhile, a person familiar with the matter said the Justice Department told the Commerce Department to pause its investigation into whether Megaspeed smuggled Nvidia’s AI chips into China. The DOJ’s request came after a Nvidia representative reached out to Commerce investigators, raising confusion about Nvidia’s involvement in the probe, the source said. Read our subscriber story for more about the Commerce Department’s investigation pause. The Justice Department’s criminal investigation into Megaspeed also focuses on whether the company smuggled Nvidia’s AI chips into China, a source said. In addition, the probe is looking at people tied to the company, like Alice Huang, and at whether China recruited her to spy and assist the smuggling of AI chips into the country. ... ## Republicans to choose new congressional leadership House and Senate Republicans are set to select their leadership teams for the new Congress, a week after a blue wave led midterm defeats. After House Speaker Mike Johnson said he wouldn’t stay on as the Republican leader, the race became a two-way contest between Majority Leader Steve Scalise and Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan, who is also the founding chairman of the hard-right House Freedom Caucus. Scalise says he can unify factions of House Republicans, while Jordan, a former Oversight Committee chairman, said he’s best positioned to combat Democratic investigations of the Trump administration. In the Senate, Majority Leader John Thune of South Dakota is running for minority leader, and so far, no one has announced plans to oppose him. But a small group of Republicans have sought to delay the elections. ... ### More election news: - California voters rejected Proposition 40, which would have imposed a one-time tax on the state’s billionaires, dealing a blow to progressives. - Trump is casting doubt on last week’s midterm results, days after saying he was “absolutely willing” to accept the Republican election losses.

items.excerpt: ## House could vote this evening on Hegseth impeachment The House could vote as early as 5:30 p.m. today on Massie's resolution to impeach Hegseth, according to the daily floor schedule. The schedule lists for possible consideration a “procedural motion relating” to the impeachment resolution, meaning a Republican could make a motion to table the resolution or refer it to a committee. Either of those votes would take a majority, and if successful, would prevent a vote on the impeachment resolution itself. If there are a majority of votes to defeat a tabling or referral motion, then the House would have to vote on the impeachment resolution. A vote on impeachment also takes a majority. Attendance will be a factor, as there were 36 members of the House absent last night during votes. Massie said yesterday that he doesn’t know if his measure has the votes to advance. NBC News has not heard from any Republicans other than Massie who have committed to backing impeachment.

Jeremy Latcham, a veteran of Marvel Studios, will take over as president and chief creative officer on Dec. 1. Gunn and Safran's projects, like “Man of Tomorrow,” will continue, but their long-term plans will no longer come to fruition. ... The assaults occurred during a time when his comedy career was taking off. A jury found him guilty of attacking four of six accusers, with allegations dating back to 2004. Prosecutors said Brand abused his fame to access women. Brand maintained his innocence, claiming all encounters were consensual. His accusers spoke about the lasting impact of his actions. Brand, known for his outrageous routines and battles with addiction, has recently focused on online content and religious discussions. Grand Theft Auto VI is almost here. items.title: Entertainment news roundup: 10 November 2026 | SVCZZ
items.excerpt: ## Box office Godzilla Minus Zero opened to $31.6 million in North America, a record debut for a live-action foreign-language film at the North American box office, according to Sunday studio estimates reported by the Associated Press. The film took about $17 million in Japan over the same weekend, and $21.3 million of its takings came from IMAX screens worldwide. The Associated Press notes the one exception among live-action films: 2004’s Passion of the Christ opened to $83.8 million. Takashi Yamazaki’s film is the sequel to Godzilla Minus One. Ramayana: Rise of a Legend earned Rs 107.50 crore net in India on day 5, Monday 9 November, its biggest single day so far and the biggest Monday ever for a Bollywood film, passing Dhurandhar 2 and its Rs 64 crore. The five-day India net stands at Rs 346.35 crore, with India gross at Rs 413.90 crore. All figures are Sacnilk estimates reported by Times Now, as of 10 November 2026. Rs 343.6 million in 17 days has made Purna Bahadur Ko Sarangi the highest-grossing Nepali film ever. Producer Binod Paudel shared the figure, which passes the previous record of Rs 235 million set by Kabaddi 4. The film also set a record single-day gross of Rs 38.9 million on 9 November 2026. Martin McDonagh’s Wild Horse Nine sits at 94 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 217 reviews, as of 10 November 2026. The espionage comedy stars John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell and is set on Easter Island shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup. It opened wide on 6 November 2026. On Rotten Tomatoes, Ramayana: Rise of a Legend holds 76 percent from 46 critic reviews, with a 90 percent verified audience score from more than 250 ratings, as of 7 November 2026. ScreenRant rated the film 7 out of 10. Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, the film stars Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, Yash and Sunny Deol. ## Trailers and first looks The trailer for Gobar Ganesh has been released at a launch event in Kathmandu. The Nepali film is directed by Marichman Shrestha and stars Balchhi Dhurbe and Barsha Siwakoti. It is scheduled for release on Magh 1. The trailer for Melania, The Series is out, ahead of the two-part docuseries reaching Prime Video on 20 November 2026. It follows the documentary film released earlier this year. A trailer is out for Darius Rucker: They Called Me Hootie, the documentary that premieres on Hulu on 16 November 2026. It traces the singer’s path from his Hootie and the Blowfish years to country stardom. Briarcliff Entertainment has released the official trailer for Drag, a dark comedy thriller starring Lizzy Caplan and Lucy DeVito as burglar sisters trapped in a home invasion. The film arrives in US theatres on 29 January 2027. Raviv Ullman and Greg Yagolnitzer directed. MGM+ has released first-look images for Bosch: Start of Watch, with Cameron Monaghan as a 26-year-old Harry Bosch in 1992 Los Angeles alongside Omari Hardwick as veteran LAPD officer Eli Bridges. The eight-episode prequel premieres on 10 January 2027 with two episodes, then weekly to the finale on 21 February. ... Daniel MacPherson has joined Priyanka Chopra Jonas and Russell Crowe in the science-fiction thriller Bluefly, playing Dugan, a Special Forces soldier. Directed by Nimrod Antal, the Congo-set film starts shooting shortly on Australia’s Gold Coast. Universal’s Snoop Dogg biopic Snoop has added Aaron Paul as music executive Jimmy Iovine, with Giovanni Ribisi joining as attorney David Kenner. Jonathan Daviss stars as Snoop, and the film opens in theatres on 6 August 2027. Halsey’s horror film Replacer has added Carrie-Anne Moss to its cast. Directed by Avan Jogia, the film has finished shooting in Montreal, Lilly Wachowski executive produces, and it has no distributor or release date yet. Halsey plays Proxy, a troubled DJ stranded in Montreal. ... Heart of the Beast arrives on digital platforms today, 10 November 2026, to rent and purchase on PVOD from 12 a.m. ET, as confirmed by Paramount Home Entertainment. The David Ayer film, starring Brad Pitt, opened in cinemas on 25 September 2026. It is Certified Fresh at 84 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 185 reviews, with a 94 percent audience score. Jessica Chastain’s supernatural horror film Other Mommy makes its digital debut today, 10 November 2026, with 4K UHD, Blu-ray and DVD following on 29 December 2026, Universal Pictures Home Entertainment has announced.
